headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend holding, short-term mood near neutral

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's posture is to scale up acquisition: both the longer trend and the last three months lean up, with medium confidence (59/100). In practice that means growing acquisition budget in measured steps rather than all at once, weighting toward active-trader and non-stablecoin channels, and keeping part of the budget flexible because the long-term average has not yet turned up and the Fed meets on 27 October. This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is 16% above its 200-day average and up 29% over 90 days.
About 61% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
The 200-day average is still sloping down (-2% over 90 days).
Price remains 33% below its all-time high of $124,753.
watch: The crowd mood reading says greed at 69, but fewer people than usual are betting on a rise with borrowed money and about $487M just left US bitcoin funds in a day. If fund money keeps leaving while price stalls below $86,603, that upbeat mood could cool quickly.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still points up, but this week looks like wait-and-see. Short term, the mood is close to neutral: the crowd mood reading is upbeat at 69/100, yet fewer people than usual are betting on a rise with borrowed money, so nothing looks overheated. News of tampered Ledger hardware wallets sold by one Southeast Asian reseller is taking a little off the mood. A daily close above $86,603 (the 30-day high) would turn this clearly up, below $81,072 (the 50-day average) it turns down, and in between expect choppy moves, so steady messaging beats urgency-driven pushes this week.

Over the next month, the lean is moderately positive: price is up about 29% over 90 days and roughly six in ten recent days closed above the long-term average. The soft spot is fund money, with about $487M leaving US bitcoin funds on the latest reported day. If price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high) the climb has room to run, while it fades if price slips below $81,072 (the 50-day average). Fund money returning would strengthen this; with the Fed meeting on 27 October, time bigger launches around that date.

Longer term, the lean is mildly positive but early: price is about 16% above its 200-day average, yet that average is still sloping down, so this is a recovery rather than a confirmed uptrend, with price still 33% below its record. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,057 (the 200-day average), with $66,544 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. The long-term average turning upward would confirm it, which is when bigger brand and onboarding investment tends to pay off most.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels with a story built on the 29% climb over three months rather than urgency, since the mood reading is already warm at 69 and the week looks choppy. The Ledger reseller scandal makes self-custody and account-security content timely; a 'how we keep your funds safe' angle can earn trust with newer and more cautious users. Keep stablecoin-first channels steady as a defensive base.

items.why: Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in a device sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, and on-chain investigators link the related thefts to around $86M, with the attacker moving about $7.45M of ETH through a mixer. Ledger's latest update says the affected devices are limited and all confirmed cases trace to that one reseller, not its own systems or direct sales.
items.marketing_angle: A timely moment for plain-language security content on buying devices from trusted sources and protecting recovery phrases.

sources.title: Ledger confirms unauthorized hardware implant found in affected user's device
Ledger: Limited number of affected devices, all confirmed cases traced to reseller CryptoBilis
Ledger incident continues to escalate: Attacker has moved $7.45 million in ETH to Tornado Cash

items.why: Starknet's STRK is up again (about 14.7% in a day and more than double over a week), joined by Wormhole, Sonic and NEAR with double-digit daily gains, though all remain far below their record highs. The reports found don't give a clear reason for these moves; a scheduled STRK token unlock next week was reported, and a NEAR-focused treasury company announced an acquisition.
items.marketing_angle: Sharp rebounds pull active traders back to smaller tokens, so simple explainers on what these networks do can catch that interest.

sources.title: Data: CRO, ARB and other tokens to see major unlocks next week, with CRO unlocking about $69.5 million

items.why: Robinhood says it is exploring stock tokens tied to actively managed ETFs with T. Rowe Price, a $1.9T asset manager. Newly launched trading venue PaperTrade says its first six hours of volume beat the stock market's over the same period, while Hyperliquid's total protocol revenue has passed $1.4B, almost all from its trading products.
items.marketing_angle: Tokenized stocks are a growing education topic for users curious about trading traditional assets around the clock.

items.theme: XRP Ledger fixes a decade-old bug
items.why: Ripple's engineering head said a serious flaw that had existed for over 10 years could have let XRP be created beyond its fixed supply; it was found through a bug bounty, never used, and fixed in version 3.4.1. The XRP Ledger Foundation stressed that no new XRP was ever created.
items.marketing_angle: Useful for reassurance content for XRP holders: the issue was caught and fixed before any harm.
